name: mosaic-token-extensions-admin
description: TypeScript SDK, CLI, and UI for managing standard token types on Solana (ex: Stablecoin & Arcade Tokens)

scripts.precommit: pnpm run format && pnpm run lint:fix
scripts.check: pnpm run build && pnpm run format:check && pnpm run lint && pnpm run type-check

author: Solana Foundation

pnpm._dependencyNotes: @solana-program/token-2022 is pinned to the PUBLISHED 0.15.0 (no tarball, no patch). 0.15.0 is the FLOOR for confidential mint/burn: it is the first release carrying the upstreamed InstructionPlan helpers (getConfidentialMintInstructionPlan / getConfidentialBurnInstructionPlan / getPermissionedConfidentialBurnInstructionPlan / getUpdateConfidentialMintBurnDecryptableSupplyInstructionFromSupply) from https://github.com/solana-program/token-2022/pull/1357 (merged 2026-08-12, shipped 2026-08-13) — 0.13.0 and 0.14.x do NOT have them. Mosaic's mint.ts/burn.ts/supply.ts delegate straight to @solana-program/token-2022/confidential; the former local proof implementation (ciphertext-math.ts / mint-burn-proof.ts / mint-burn-util.ts, on @noble/curves) is deleted, and @noble/curves is now an internal token-2022 dependency rather than a Mosaic one. Also note token-2022 must be >=0.13.0 on kit v7 regardless: 0.12.0's compiled code imports getMinimumBalanceForRentExemption from @solana/kit, which kit v7 removed. 0.15.0 additionally moves two peers, which is why the pins below moved with it: @solana/zk-sdk to ^0.5.1 (purely additive vs 0.4.2 — it only adds a ConfidentialKeys class, which does not collide with Mosaic's same-named type because zk-sdk is re-exported only through the separate @solana/mosaic-sdk/_zk subpath) and @solana-program/zk-elgamal-proof to ^0.3.2 (every symbol confidential/proof.ts imports still exists, and 0.3.2 declares kit ^7 natively). @solana/token-acl-sdk@0.4.0 declares an exact token-2022 0.12.0 dependency; the override forces it up to 0.15.0 — safe because it only consumes stable core exports (TOKEN_2022_PROGRAM_ADDRESS, getMintDecoder, ATA/metadata helpers, AccountState, Mint), unchanged across 0.10-0.15. @solana/token-acl-sdk / @solana/token-acl-gate-sdk / @solana/connector declare kit <=6 peer ranges but run correctly on kit v7 (they only touch codecs/signers/addresses; the only v7 breaking changes — a type-only codec-union return-type widening, ReactiveStreamStore.connect(), a new instruction-planning error — are not exercised) and are forced onto v7 via the @solana/kit + @solana/* overrides. @solana-program/system and @solana-program/memo are on their kit-v7-native releases (0.13.0 / 0.12.0). See packages/sdk/package.json `_dependencyNotes`. NO PATCHES: nothing in this repo is `pnpm patch`ed any more. Historically @solana/zk-sdk WAS patched (through 0.5.1) to make its ./bundler subpath condition-aware, because token-2022's confidential.mjs hardcodes `@solana/zk-sdk/bundler` (the ESM+wasm bundler build) which can't load under Node (`Unknown file extension .wasm`) and, if forced, yields a dual-WASM `expected instance of ElGamalKeypair` mismatch. @solana/zk-sdk 0.5.2 (published 2026-08-27) ships that fix upstream — https://github.com/solana-program/zk-elgamal-proof/pull/519 added a `node` condition on ./bundler (pointing at the CJS node build, with types) AND a condition-aware root `.` export plus a `main` field, which was the stated removal criterion for the patch. 0.5.2 is otherwise byte-identical to 0.5.1 (dist/node/*, dist/bundler/*, dist/web/index.js all unchanged): the release is packaging metadata only, zero API change. The zk-sdk override REMAINS pinned exactly (0.5.2, not ^0.5.2) for a different reason than before — it guarantees exactly ONE resolved zk-sdk copy across the tree; a second copy reintroduces the dual-WASM class-identity mismatch. The corresponding packages/sdk/jest.config.js `@solana/zk-sdk/bundler` remap is likewise removed: jest runs with testEnvironment 'node' and now honours the upstream `node` condition on its own. NOTE: packages/sdk/src/confidential/_zk.{node,browser}.ts and the `./_zk` export in packages/sdk/package.json are NOT workarounds and must stay — they are Mosaic's own deliberate build-selection indirection.
